question.text: What national wholesale price for graded, loose, white Large shell eggs will the USDA AMS Egg Markets Overview dated November 13, 2026 report? (cents per dozen)
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the single price stated in the USDA AMS "Egg Markets Overview" report dated November 13, 2026, in the sentence reporting the "wholesale prices for national trading of truck lot quantities of graded, loose, white Large shell eggs" (the sentence typically reads like "Wholesale prices for national trading of truck lot quantities of graded, loose, white Large shell eggs were $0.01 lower at $0.28 per dozen with a steady undertone"). The edition is available from the AMS report archive at https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/3725 (select the 2026 releases and open the November 13, 2026 PDF) and, on its publication day, at https://www.ams.usda.gov/mnreports/ams_3725.pdf. The value is expressed in cents per dozen: a report stating "$0.35 per dozen" resolves as 35, and a report stating "35 cents per dozen" also resolves as 35. Only that one price counts; other prices in the same report (New York formula cartoned, Midwest warehouse-delivered, Midwest producer, California benchmarks, breaking stock, egg products) are disregarded.
question.fine_print: If the edition dated November 13, 2026 is not published, or is published without this line, this question resolves to the value for the same line in the next edition of the Egg Markets Overview that reports it. If the report stops publishing this line entirely and no later edition reports it, the question is annulled.

research:
I couldn't confirm a November 6 edition. The latest one I could check is dated October 30, 2026, which reported 35¢. Nothing has happened yet that settles the question.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-30: the Egg Markets Overview reported national truck-lot graded loose white Large at **$0.35/dozen, up $0.07, steady undertone**. Other figures in that edition: NY formula $0.72 (steady), Midwest warehouse-delivered $0.54 (steady), California $1.10 (up $0.09), average conventional ad price $1.42 (up $0.10), national Large inventory up 11%, breaking stock $0.08 (down $0.025), Weekly Shell Egg Demand Indicator -4.70 (down 8.3 points). IndexBox published this summary on 2026-11-02. [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-egg-markets-overview-mixed-weekly-egg-prices-as-inventories-rise/)
- 2026-11-03: the live PDF ([ams_3725.pdf](https://www.ams.usda.gov/mnreports/ams_3725.pdf)) came back as binary I couldn't read. Search results showed its headline as "Negotiated wholesale prices for graded loose caged eggs were steady to lower"; I couldn't tell which edition that headline belongs to. The [archive page](https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/3725) timed out.

### 2. Current status
- Not settled. The report is due Friday 2026-11-13.
- 2026-11-02: in the AMS Daily National Shell Egg Index (a 5-day rolling average), national caged graded loose white Large had a **weighted average of 35.42¢, up 0.52¢** from 34.90¢. The range was 21 to 54¢ on 25,728 cases, and the year-ago figure was 163.78¢. Undertone was steady to firm, supplies moderate to fully adequate, retail demand moderate, loose-egg demand light. Total shell egg inventory was reported up 3.9%. This daily series appears to track the weekly line closely (35¢ on 10/30). [IndexBox daily](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-daily-shell-egg-index-report-national-prices-steady-to-higher-on-2-november-2026/), [AMS 2843](https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/2843)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: daily index described as steady to higher, with Large near 35¢ (see above).
- 2026-10-29: Iowa reported its first commercial HPAI case of 2026, a 45,000-bird turkey flock. It is not a layer flock. [WATTPoultry](https://www.wattagnet.com/poultry-meat/diseases-health/avian-influenza/news/16274660/iowa-confirms-first-commercial-hpai-case-of-2026)
- 2026-10-28: about 1.3 million layers in Stanislaus County, CA were confirmed with HPAI, the second large layer outbreak in three weeks. [WATTPoultry](https://www.wattagnet.com/poultry-meat/diseases-health/avian-influenza/news/16050490/13-million-california-laying-hens-struck-by-avian-flu)
- 2026-10-19 (one source says Oct 9): 934,600 layers in Clinton County, IL, reportedly a Rose Acre Farms operation. [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/science/articles/nearly-1-million-chickens-slaughtered-153059381.html)
- 2026-09-02: an American Egg Board outlook said supply continues to outpace strong demand, wholesale prices are depressed, and elevated supply is expected through 2026 and into 2027. [Feedstuffs](https://www.feedstuffs.com/market-news/egg-demand-remains-strong-in-august-2026)
- I found no layer-flock HPAI detection in November 2026.

### 4. Base rates
- Recent weekly values in cents (from the question background): 9/4: 35, 9/18: 35, 9/25: 39, 10/9: 43, 10/16: 29, 10/23: 28, 10/30: 35. The 2026 range runs from 24 (mid-June) to about 151 (March).
- Typical weekly moves are 1 to 7¢. Moves of 14 to 37¢ have happened several times in 2026. The two weeks between 10/30 and 11/13 add up two weekly moves, so a change of plus or minus 10 to 15¢ is plausible without a shock.
- Seasonal pattern: AMS describes Thanksgiving baking as the year's biggest shell-egg demand period. A 2019 AMS analysis found pre-Thanksgiving wholesale prices up to 19% above pre-Christmas levels. [AMS 2019](https://www.ams.usda.gov/mnreports/pyathanksgiving.pdf), [Poultry Times](https://www.poultrytimes.com/?p=17496)
- Year-ago comparison: the early-November 2025 daily Large figure was about 164¢, so prices are now much lower year over year.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on this AMS line. The related Kalshi markets are:
  - "Egg prices up in October?" (a CPI-type measure): Yes at 0.33.
  - Egg McMuffin price in November: "At least $4.80" at 0.72.
  - Neither one maps directly onto the loose wholesale price.
- I found no expert forecast for November 2026. Expana and Urner Barry quotes are behind paywalls and turned up nothing.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-06 (Fri): the next Egg Markets Overview, which gives the trend one week before resolution.
- Daily AMS 2843 index each business day, the best real-time proxy (about 35¢ as of 11/2).
- Any APHIS layer detections ([APHIS](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/h5n1-hpai), [The Scramble tracker](https://the-scramble.com/hpai/layer-flocks)). The depopulations in Illinois and California may tighten supply as they work through.
- Pre-Thanksgiving retail features (Thanksgiving is 11/26) against large inventories: Large stocks were up 11% and the flock was up about 5% year over year.
- 2026-11-11 (Wed, Veterans Day): a federal holiday. I haven't verified whether it could shift report timing.
- The NASS Chickens and Eggs report (around 11/20) and the ERS outlook (around 11/17) both come out after resolution.

## Research summary: USDA AMS Egg Markets Overview, November 13, 2026, national loose white Large price

The latest weekly figure is 35¢/dozen (October 30), and the daily 5-day index is about the same at 35.42¢ (November 2), with a "steady to firm" undertone. Nothing settles the question yet. The November 6 edition is the next reading.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: I fetched the live report PDF (ams_3725.pdf), but it came back as unreadable compressed binary, so I could not confirm which edition is posted. A search snippet of the same URL showed "$0.03 lower at $0.43 per dozen". That matches the October 9 edition and is probably a stale cached copy. [AMS](https://www.ams.usda.gov/mnreports/ams_3725.pdf)
- 2026-10-30 edition, as summarized by IndexBox:
  - National loose white Large was **35¢, up 7¢, steady undertone**.
  - New York cartoned Large held at 72¢ and Midwest warehouse-delivered at 54¢.
  - The California benchmark rose 9¢ to $1.10.
  - Shell egg inventory was up 7%, and national Large inventory up 11%.
  - The Weekly Shell Egg Demand Indicator was -4.70, down 8.3 points.
  - For the period ending Nov 5, the retail Feature Rate rose 5.1% and the Activity Index rose 17%.
  - [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-egg-markets-overview-mixed-weekly-egg-prices-as-inventories-rise/)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles or nearly settles the outcome. The November 6 edition is not out yet, and the November 13 edition is still 10 days away.
- 2026-11-02: The Daily National Shell Egg Index (5-day rolling average, report 2843) put caged graded loose white Large at **35.42¢**, up 0.52¢ from 34.90¢. [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-daily-shell-egg-index-report-national-prices-steady-to-higher-on-2-november-2026/)
  - Range 21 to 54¢, about 25.7k cases traded. The year-ago figure was 163.78¢.
  - Undertone "steady to firm, lightly tested". Retail demand moderate, loose-egg demand light, supplies moderate to fully adequate.
  - Cage-free loose Large was 44.17¢ (+4.00¢). California delivered loose Large was 65.27¢ (+5.44¢), with a "firm to higher" undertone.
- I could not find the November 3 daily index. [AMS 2843](https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/2843)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: IndexBox reported a total shell egg inventory of 1,653.1 thousand 30-dozen cases, up 3.9% (it describes this as the week of Nov 2). [IndexBox search result](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-organic-poultry-and-eggs-report-november-2-2026-market-conditions/)
- 2026-10-28: HPAI was confirmed in a 1.3M-bird layer flock in Stanislaus County, California. This likely explains the strength in California prices. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/hpai/layer-flocks)
- 2026-10-19: HPAI was confirmed in a 934,600-bird layer flock in Clinton County, Illinois. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/hpai/layer-flocks)
- Through 2026-10-28: there have been 15 layer detections in 7 states in 2026, about 18.3M birds. The only detections since July 6 are the two above. I found no US layer detections dated November 2026.
- 2026-10-27: The Netherlands had its first layer outbreak of the 2026/27 season, which is not directly relevant to US prices. [WUR](https://www.wur.nl/en/news/first-poultry-farm-tests-positive-avian-influenza)
- The articles from the news API (Egypt and Spain egg prices) are not relevant to the US AMS series.

### 4. Base rates
- Recent weekly values in ¢/dozen:
  - Sep 4: 35
  - Sep 18: 35
  - Sep 25: 39
  - Oct 9: 43
  - Oct 16: 29
  - Oct 23: 28
  - Oct 30: 35
- Two-week changes, the same horizon as Oct 30 to Nov 13, using the background data:

| From | To | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Sep 4 | Sep 18 | 0¢ |
| Sep 25 | Oct 9 | +4¢ |
| Oct 9 | Oct 23 | -15¢ |
| Oct 16 | Oct 30 | +6¢ |

- The only bigger example I have, Feb 27 to early March, was a 37¢ jump in one week during an HPAI-driven spike.
- The 2026 range is about 24¢ (mid-June low) to about 151¢ (March high).
- The current level of about 35¢ sits near the bottom of that range.
- The 5-day daily index, now 35.42¢, has historically tracked the weekly loose figure closely, which makes it a useful leading read.
- I could not verify the November 2025 seasonal pattern for this specific line.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on the AMS loose Large price.
- The Kalshi markets provided are only loosely related:
  - "Egg prices up in October?" (CPI-type, retail) trades at 0.33 Yes.
  - Egg McMuffin price and chicken wing wholesale price markets are not relevant.
- I found no expert point forecasts for mid-November wholesale loose eggs. USDA ERS expects 2026 retail egg prices to end about 29% below 2025, according to a secondary tracker. [coopeduplife](https://coopeduplife.com/egg-prices/)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Daily index (AMS 2843), every business day:** the most direct leading indicator. [AMS 2843](https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/2843)
- **2026-11-06:** Egg Markets Overview, the last weekly reading before resolution.
- **About 2026-11-10 to 11-12:** BLS October CPI, including retail egg prices.
- **2026-11-13 (Friday afternoon, Central time):** the resolving edition.
- **Ongoing risks:** new HPAI layer detections tracked by [APHIS](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/h5n1-hpai) and The Scramble, plus Thanksgiving (Nov 26) baking and retail feature demand. Rising inventories (+7% week over week, Midwest Large +19%) push the other way.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. The November 13, 2026 edition is due Friday afternoon Central time, around 22:00 UTC.

(b) **Latest known value:** 35¢/dozen in the October 30, 2026 edition, up 7¢ with a steady undertone. The daily AMS index on November 2 showed a weighted average of 35.42¢ with a steady to firm undertone. That daily series is a 5-day rolling average, not the resolving line.

(c) **If nothing changed:** About 35¢.

(d) **If the trend continued:** The trend is mildly upward. The October 30 edition was up 7¢ and the daily index is drifting up. Pre-Thanksgiving demand is building, and recent layer losses in Illinois and California (about 2.2 million hens) will feed through. Against that, large inventories (Large up 11%) and a flock up 5% year over year cap the rise. Continuing the trend gives roughly 38 to 45¢.

(e) **Historical variation:** Two weekly moves add up before resolution. Typical moves are 1 to 7¢ a week, with occasional 14 to 37¢ swings. A two-week change of plus or minus 10 to 15¢ is plausible, and larger moves happen in shocks. The 2026 range is 24 to about 151¢.

(f) **Experts and markets:** No market covers this line. The American Egg Board expects supply to stay elevated and wholesale prices depressed through 2026. The seasonal pattern favors firmness before Thanksgiving. Taken together, these point to modest upside rather than a spike.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Pre-Thanksgiving buying finishes early, inventories keep building, and loose eggs get dumped onto the spot market. The price falls back to the mid-20s, as low as about 20¢, near the June low.
- **High:** Several large new layer HPAI detections hit in early November on top of the Illinois and California depopulations. Combined with holiday demand, the negotiated loose price could jump 30 to 60¢, as in March, reaching 80 to 100¢ or more.
